free_tier.stated: no request count and no key: an absolute maximum of 1 request per second per application, summed over all its users; a script running longer than a day or at regular intervals is held to 4 requests per minute, from a single thread on one machine
free_tier.notes: a rate ceiling, not a metered quota; the service runs on donated servers with a very limited capacity, and the policy may change without notice

per_object_cap.stated: one query per request, returning at most 40 results

retention.notes: the answer carries the licence line "Data © OpenStreetMap contributors"

egress.terms: not applicable: a query API, not metered in bytes

interface_detail: HTTPS GET to nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search (and /reverse, /lookup) with format=json, jsonv2, geojson, geocodejson or xml; no key; a valid HTTP Referer or an application User-Agent is required; without a format parameter the public instance answers with the web page
tooling: any HTTP client that sets an identifying User-Agent or Referer; the policy asks apps to go through a caching proxy
chaining: a keyless geocoder for low-volume, user-triggered lookups at 1 request a second; a stored data set of more than a few thousand addresses goes to a keyed provider with storable results (data-apis/geoapify, data-apis/opencage, data-apis/maptiler). Bulk path: no bulk geocoding (systematic queries are banned); the raw data is the weekly OSM planet file (89 GB PBF) or a regional extract. The last resort is self-hosted: the Nominatim software, which the user installs and runs on a rented machine with an imported planet or extract

limits.value: 1 request per second at most, summed over every user of an application
4 requests per minute for a script that runs longer than a day or at regular intervals; one thread on one machine
at most 40 results for one search

limits_note: auto-complete search, systematic queries (reverse queries in a grid, complete lists of postcodes or towns, all POIs in an area) and scraping of the details page are banned outright
binding_note: there is no counted quota, so the 1 request per second ceiling, and 4 per minute for a long-running script, is the whole capacity

identity_cost.detail: no account and no key; each request carries a valid HTTP Referer or a User-Agent that identifies the application, since stock library User-Agents are refused by the policy

reliability_note: a requester that sends the same query repeatedly may be classed as faulty and blocked, a banned use (auto-complete, systematic queries, scraping of the details page) leads to a ban, and access can be withdrawn when the definition of heavy use changes
confidence_note: the rate ceiling is documented and was not exercised.
